skills.description: Current assets minus current liabilities, and the cycle that shows how many days cash is tied up between paying suppliers and collecting from customers.

skills.name: Inventory & Supply Chain Fundamentals
skills.description: The tradeoff between ordering too often (higher ordering cost) and ordering too much (higher holding cost) that sits behind every inventory decision.

skills.name: Budgeting Basics & the Master Budget
skills.description: What a budget is for, and how individual budgets (sales, labor, materials) roll up into one master budget for the year.

skills.name: Management Reporting & Variance Basics
skills.description: How internal reports differ from external financial statements, and the basic mechanics of comparing actual results to budget.

skills.name: Business Entity Types & Contract Basics
skills.description: How a business is legally organized changes who's liable, how it's taxed, and what a contract with it can bind.

skills.name: Tax Basics for a Business
skills.description: The handful of tax types (income, self-employment, employment) a business owner or finance employee needs to recognize, even without doing the filing.

skills.name: Excel Quick-Start for Finance
skills.description: Just enough Excel -- SUM, AVERAGE, IF, a lookup function -- to build the small models used throughout this course. Dedicated Excel tracks go far deeper than this.

skills.name: PowerPoint Basics for Presenting Numbers
skills.description: Enough PowerPoint mechanics to turn an analysis into a handful of clear slides.

skills.name: Business Writing for Numbers
skills.description: Turning an analysis into a short, clear written summary a busy reader can act on.

skills.name: Ratio Analysis & DuPont Decomposition
skills.description: Break return on equity into its profitability, efficiency and leverage drivers with DuPont analysis, and use the full ratio toolkit to judge a company's financial health.

skills.name: Common-Size and Trend Analysis
skills.description: Normalize statements to a base (common-size/vertical analysis) and compare periods (horizontal/trend analysis) to spot structural shifts a raw dollar figure hides.

skills.name: Cash Flow Analysis, Working Capital & the Cash Conversion Cycle
skills.description: Analyze how efficiently a company turns sales into cash: working capital mechanics, and the cash conversion cycle as the standard lens on that efficiency.

skills.name: Budgeting Approaches & the Annual Planning Cycle
skills.description: Understand how companies build an annual budget, the main budgeting methods and their trade-offs, and how actuals get checked against plan.

skills.name: 13-Week and Monthly Cash-Flow Forecasting
skills.description: Build short-term liquidity forecasts the way treasury and FP&A teams actually run them: the direct-method 13-week rolling forecast and the monthly indirect-method view.

skills.name: Scenario & Sensitivity Analysis
skills.description: Test which assumptions actually move a model's output using Excel data tables and a scenario manager, and present the results so a decision-maker can act on them.

skills.name: Model Structure, Design & Best Practices
skills.description: Learn the conventions that make a model intuitive and error-resistant: consistent formatting, separating inputs from calculations from outputs, and documenting assumptions.

skills.name: Driver-Based Forecasting: Revenue & Cost Builds
skills.description: Forecast revenue and cost of goods sold from operating drivers (price, volume, mix) rather than a flat growth rate, and know when a bottom-up build is worth the extra effort.

skills.name: Supporting Schedules: PP&E, Working Capital, Debt & Equity
skills.description: Build the schedules that feed a 3-statement model: a PP&E roll-forward, working-capital and balance-sheet line forecasts, and a debt schedule with interest and mandatory repayments.

skills.name: Circularity, Balancing & Model Auditing
skills.description: Understand why circular references appear once debt and interest are linked together, how to handle them safely, and how to audit a finished model for errors before anyone relies on it.

skills.name: EV-to-Equity Bridge & the Treasury Stock Method
skills.description: Bridge enterprise value to equity value correctly, and use the treasury stock method to convert dilutive options and warrants into a fully diluted share count.

skills.name: Terminal Value, Mid-Year Convention & Stub Periods
skills.description: Choose between the Gordon growth and exit multiple terminal value methods, cross-check one against the other, and apply mid-year discounting and stub periods without silently mixing conventions.

skills.name: Valuation Synthesis: the Football Field
skills.description: Bring DCF, comps and precedent transactions together into a single football field chart that shows the range and the overlap across methods.

skills.name: Data Visualization Principles for Financial Reporting
skills.description: Choose the right chart for the message, and apply the principles that make a financial visual persuasive rather than merely decorative.

skills.name: Building Interactive Finance Dashboards in Excel
skills.description: Build a working Excel dashboard with pivot tables, slicers and sparklines that lets a viewer explore variance without touching a formula.

skills.name: Financial Storytelling & Data Narrative
skills.description: Turn a set of numbers into a structured narrative that leads an audience from context to insight to recommended action.

skills.name: Business & Financial Writing
skills.description: Write the memo, executive summary or email that gets a busy reader to the decision quickly: lead with the conclusion, and cut every sentence that doesn't earn its place.

skills.name: Presenting Finance to Leadership & Building the Deck
skills.description: Structure a management presentation the way a finance team actually builds one, and use PowerPoint efficiently enough to iterate under deadline pressure.

skills.name: Acquisition Underwriting: Income Capitalization & Pro Forma
skills.description: Go beyond the REIT-level FFO/AFFO view (fin-p14-t2) into deal-level underwriting: build a property-level pro forma and value it off NOI and a market cap rate the way an acquisitions analyst does.

skills.name: Debt Sizing & Real Estate Equity Waterfalls
skills.description: Size acquisition debt the way a CRE lender does (DSCR, debt yield, loan constant), then build the promote structure that splits a deal's profit between the sponsor and LP investors across return tiers.

skills.name: Ground-Up Development: Land Residual & Construction Pro Forma
skills.description: Model a development deal from raw land: back into a maximum land price with a residual land value analysis, then build the construction-phase cash flow and lease-up that feeds the stabilized pro forma.

skills.name: Mining Valuation: Reserves Classification, NAV & Price Decks
skills.description: Mining assets are valued by summing the discounted cash flows of each individual mine (a NAV, sum-of-the-parts approach), driven off reserve/resource classification and a metal price deck rather than a revenue multiple.

skills.name: Oil & Gas Modelling: Decline Curves, Type Curves & NAV
skills.description: An E&P company's production declines to zero as its wells deplete, so revenue is modelled off a decline curve rather than a growth assumption, and the company is valued as a NAV of its existing and type-curve-driven future wells.

skills.name: Commodity Price Decks & Sensitivity Analysis
skills.description: The commodity price deck is usually the single most debated input in a natural-resources model, so build the scenario structure (strip, consensus, management, bull/bear) and the two-way sensitivity tables that stress-test it.

skills.name: Renewable Power Project Modelling: PPA & Capacity Factor
skills.description: A solar or wind project's revenue is production (driven by capacity factor) times a contracted PPA price, not a market-priced merchant curve, which is what lets it be financed with cheap, highly-levered non-recourse debt.

skills.name: Advanced Project Finance: CFADS & Debt Sculpting
skills.description: Go beyond the single DSCR/LLCR sizing pass in fin-p14-t3: build Cash Flow Available for Debt Service (CFADS) precisely, then sculpt principal repayment period by period so the DSCR sits exactly at its covenant floor across the loan life.

skills.name: Infrastructure & PPP Modelling
skills.description: Public infrastructure that has no user-fee revenue of its own (a courthouse, a school) is financed instead against a government's availability payment, a fixed obligation once the asset is certified ready for use.

skills.name: SaaS & Tech: Cohort Analysis, Unit Economics & ARR
skills.description: Model a subscription business off ARR, cohort-level retention and the LTV/CAC relationship rather than a traditional revenue build, and know which multiple (ARR vs. revenue) the market actually prices it on.

skills.name: E-Commerce & Marketplace Revenue Modelling
skills.description: A marketplace's real top line is GMV, not revenue: model gross merchandise volume, the take rate that converts it into revenue, and liquidity — and know why quoting GMV as revenue overstates the business.

skills.name: Consumer, Retail & Restaurant Unit Economics
skills.description: Chains are valued store by store: same-store sales isolates organic growth from new-unit growth, and four-wall economics and payback period decide whether opening the next unit creates value.

skills.name: Healthcare & Biotech: rNPV and Pipeline Valuation
skills.description: A clinical-stage biotech has no revenue and a high chance of failure, so its pipeline is valued with risk-adjusted NPV: probability-weight each drug's cash flows by phase before discounting, rather than assuming they arrive with certainty.

skills.name: Full LBO Build: Sources & Uses to Returns Attribution
skills.description: Go past the single-tranche LBO in fin-p8-t2 into what a real deal looks like: a multi-tranche debt stack with different pricing and amortization on each piece, and a formal returns-attribution bridge that decomposes IRR into deleveraging, EBITDA growth and multiple expansion.

skills.name: Paper LBO & Quick IRR Math
skills.description: A PE interview routinely asks for an LBO's IRR with no Excel and five minutes: build the mental-math shortcuts (Rule of 72/115) that get you a Sources & Uses table and an approximate return in your head.

skills.name: Advanced Merger Model: PPA & Pro-Forma Balance Sheet
skills.description: Extend the accretion/dilution model in fin-p5-t3 with purchase price allocation: revalue the target's assets to fair value, calculate the resulting goodwill, and consolidate both companies' balance sheets on day one.

skills.name: Contribution Analysis, SOTP & Fairness Opinions
skills.description: Round out the deal-modelling toolkit with the frameworks used on complex or contested transactions: contribution analysis to set ownership splits in a merger of equals, sum-of-the-parts to value a conglomerate, and the fairness opinion a board relies on to approve a deal.

skills.name: Fund Cash Flow Modelling: Capital Calls & the J-Curve
skills.description: Build the fund-level cash flow model itself, not just the waterfall concepts in fin-p9-t4: a commitment-pacing schedule, capital calls, fee accrual and distributions that together produce the fund's characteristic J-shaped cash flow curve.

skills.name: Return Metrics: IRR vs MOIC vs DPI/TVPI
skills.description: Calculate the four numbers every LP asks a GP for, and know when each one is the right answer: IRR (time-weighted), MOIC (magnitude only), and DPI/TVPI (cash returned vs. total value, realized vs. unrealized).

skills.name: Cap Tables, Dilution & Liquidation Preferences
skills.description: Go past the thesis-and-term-sheet view in fin-p9-t3 into the actual math: build a cap table across financing rounds, calculate dilution including the option pool shuffle, and model how a liquidation preference stack pays out at exit.

skills.name: Revenue Recognition (ASC 606 / IFRS 15)
skills.description: The five-step model that now governs revenue recognition under both US GAAP and IFRS — identifying the contract and performance obligations, pricing them, and timing recognition to when control transfers, not when cash is collected.

skills.name: Leases (ASC 842 / IFRS 16)
skills.description: Since 2019 almost every lease sits on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. Learn the classification test, the journal entries, and why finance and operating leases still hit the income statement differently under US GAAP.

skills.name: Deferred Tax, NOLs & Stock-Based Compensation
skills.description: Three line items that separate GAAP earnings from cash and from each other: the deferred tax assets and liabilities that arise when book and tax timing diverge, the NOLs a loss-making company carries forward, and the non-cash stock compensation expense that dilutes shareholders without ever touching cash flow.

skills.name: Consolidation, NCI & the Equity Method
skills.description: Three ways to account for an equity stake depending on control: cost method below 20%, equity method for 20-50% influence, and full consolidation with a non-controlling interest line above 50%. Get the thresholds and the mechanics of each.

skills.name: Goodwill, Purchase Price Allocation & Impairment
skills.description: What happens to the balance sheet the day after an acquisition closes: fair-valuing the target's assets, booking the residual as goodwill, and testing that goodwill for impairment every year after.

skills.name: Pensions & Post-Employment Benefits
skills.description: Defined benefit plans put a long-dated, discount-rate-sensitive liability on the balance sheet and a multi-part expense on the income statement — service cost, interest cost, and the return on plan assets, all before a single benefit is paid.

skills.name: IFRS vs US GAAP vs Ind AS
skills.description: The framework differences that matter for cross-border comparability: LIFO, development-cost capitalisation, cash flow classification, and the specific carve-outs India's Ind AS makes from the IFRS it is based on.

skills.name: Bond Pricing, Yields & the Yield Curve
skills.description: A bond's price is the present value of its coupons and principal at the market yield. Learn to price a bond from its cash flows, read yield to maturity as an IRR, and plot the yield curve that every other rate in the market is set relative to.

skills.name: Duration, Convexity & Interest Rate Risk
skills.description: Duration approximates how much a bond's price moves for a 1% change in rates; convexity corrects for the fact that relationship curves rather than moves in a straight line. Together they are how a fixed-income desk sizes interest-rate risk.

skills.name: Credit Spreads & Relative Value
skills.description: The spread over a government benchmark is the market's price for a bond's default risk. Learn to read spread levels and spread widening or tightening as a signal, and how a credit investor decides one bond is cheap relative to another.

skills.name: Credit Rating Methodology & the Rating Scale
skills.description: What AAA through D actually mean, and how an agency gets from a company's financials to a letter grade — the scorecard, the qualitative overlay, and the investment-grade/speculative-grade line that decides who is allowed to buy the bond.

skills.name: Loan & Credit Agreement Mechanics
skills.description: What is actually in the document that governs a loan: maintenance versus incurrence covenants, why cov-lite structures shifted market power to borrowers, and what a lender can and cannot do when a covenant is breached.

skills.name: Forwards, Futures & Cost-of-Carry Pricing
skills.description: Why a forward or futures price is what it is: the no-arbitrage relationship between spot price, the cost of financing and holding the underlying, and any income it throws off in between.

skills.name: Swap Valuation
skills.description: How the fixed and floating legs of an interest rate swap are each valued as a bond, why the swap is worth zero at inception, and how its mark-to-market value moves as rates move afterward.

skills.name: Option Pricing: Binomial Trees & Black-Scholes
skills.description: The two ways an option actually gets priced: a discrete binomial lattice that a spreadsheet can build step by step, and the closed-form Black-Scholes formula the lattice converges to as the steps shrink.

skills.name: Real Options in Capital Budgeting
skills.description: A standard NPV ignores the value of managerial flexibility. Real options — to defer, expand, contract or abandon a project — apply option-pricing logic to that flexibility, and can make an uncertain project more valuable, not less.

skills.name: Cash & Liquidity Management
skills.description: Treasury's daily job: make sure cash is in the right entity, the right currency and the right account to meet every obligation that falls due, while putting idle cash to short-term use.

skills.name: FX Exposure & Hedging
skills.description: A company that sells or sources across currencies is short or long FX whether it hedges or not. Learn to separate transaction, translation and economic exposure, and hedge the one that actually threatens cash flow.

skills.name: Interest Rate Risk Management for Corporates
skills.description: A borrower with floating-rate debt is exposed to rising rates; one with fixed-rate debt is exposed to being stuck above market if rates fall. Learn how corporates use swaps and caps to manage that trade-off.

skills.name: CAPM, Factor Models & the Efficient Frontier
skills.description: Markowitz's efficient frontier shows the best risk-return trade-offs diversification can buy; CAPM reduces that to one systematic-risk factor, and multi-factor models like Fama-French add size, value and other factors to explain far more of a portfolio's return.

skills.name: Asset Allocation & Performance Attribution
skills.description: Once a portfolio has beaten (or lagged) its benchmark, attribution decomposes why: how much came from over- or under-weighting sectors versus picking better securities within them.

skills.name: Regression & Statistical Methods for Finance
skills.description: Beta, factor loadings and correlation are all regression outputs. Learn to run and interpret a linear regression in a finance context, and to compute the covariance-based beta by hand as well as in Excel.

skills.name: Monte Carlo Simulation, VaR/ES & Stress Testing
skills.description: Three ways to answer 'how bad could this get': simulate thousands of random paths, summarize the loss distribution's tail as a VaR or expected-shortfall number, and run a specific adverse scenario end to end.

skills.name: Macroeconomics for Finance Professionals
skills.description: The handful of macro indicators every desk watches: GDP growth, inflation, and the policy rate a central bank sets in response to both — and how each one moves through to equity, credit and FX markets.

skills.name: ESG & Sustainable Finance
skills.description: How environmental, social and governance factors entered mainstream investment analysis: the UN-backed principles investors sign onto, the regulatory push behind disclosure, and where ESG genuinely changes a valuation versus where it is a label.

skills.name: Ethics & Professional Standards
skills.description: The code that governs the profession when no regulator is watching: duty to clients, independence and objectivity, and the standards that decide what a real conflict of interest looks like versus a manageable one.

skills.description: Recognise when a model fabricates facts, use grounding techniques to anchor responses in verified sources, and write verification prompts.

skills.description: Understand data-privacy considerations, bias risks, and organisational policies for deploying AI tools in professional settings.

skills.description: Learn the building blocks of every automation: what fires a workflow, what it does, and how conditions filter which runs proceed.

skills.description: Apply a simple decision framework to identify repetitive, rule-based tasks in your work that are high-value automation targets.

skills.description: Call the Anthropic API using the Python SDK, explore available Claude models, and compare response formats with OpenAI's output.

skills.name: Chains and Prompt Templates

skills.name: Memory and Conversation History
skills.description: Add conversation memory to your chains so the LLM can reference prior turns, and choose the right memory type for your context-length budget.

skills.name: Document Loaders and Text Splitters
skills.description: Load PDFs, web pages, and text files into LangChain, split them into manageable chunks, and prepare them for embedding.

skills.name: What Are Vector Embeddings?
skills.description: Understand how text is converted to high-dimensional vectors, what semantic similarity means numerically, and why embeddings power modern search.

skills.name: Setting Up FAISS and Chroma
skills.description: Index a document collection in FAISS (in-memory) and Chroma (persistent), and compare their trade-offs for development versus production.

skills.name: Similarity Search in Practice
skills.description: Run k-nearest-neighbour queries against a vector store, tune top-k and score thresholds, and inspect retrieved chunks for relevance.

skills.name: RAG Architecture End-to-End
skills.description: Wire together document loading, embedding, vector storage, retrieval, and answer generation into a complete RAG pipeline.

skills.name: Chunking Strategies
skills.description: Compare fixed-size, recursive, semantic, and sentence-window chunking strategies and measure how each affects retrieval quality.

skills.name: Reranking and Retrieval Optimization
skills.description: Apply a cross-encoder reranker after initial retrieval, use MMR for diversity, and evaluate the pipeline with simple hit-rate metrics.

skills.description: Build a ReAct agent that alternates reasoning steps with tool calls, observe the Thought/Action/Observation loop in LangChain's executor.

skills.description: Create an agent that can search the web, read pages, and synthesise an answer to a research question using a chain of tool calls.

skills.name: Streamlit for LLM Demos
skills.description: Build an interactive web UI for your RAG pipeline using Streamlit — add a chat interface, file upload, and source citations in under 100 lines.

skills.name: LangSmith Tracing and Debugging
skills.description: Connect LangSmith to your LangChain application, trace every chain run, inspect intermediate steps, and compare prompt versions.

skills.name: Cost Monitoring and Optimization
skills.description: Track token usage and API spend, apply prompt caching and model-selection strategies, and set budget guardrails for production workloads.

skills.description: Write your first queries — choose columns with SELECT, filter rows with WHERE, and sort results with ORDER BY.

skills.name: GROUP BY, HAVING, and Aggregate Functions
skills.description: Summarise datasets with COUNT, SUM, and AVG, group them with GROUP BY, and filter groups with the HAVING clause.

skills.name: Databases vs. Spreadsheets
skills.description: Understand when SQL beats Excel — relational structure, millions of rows, reproducibility, and the limits of each tool.

skills.name: INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN
skills.description: Combine rows from two tables on a shared key using INNER JOIN (matched rows only) and LEFT JOIN (all left-table rows).

skills.name: RIGHT, FULL, and Multi-Table JOINs
skills.description: Complete the JOIN family with RIGHT and FULL OUTER JOINs, then chain multiple JOINs to pull data from three or more tables at once.

skills.description: Power Query's four-phase model — Connect, Transform, Combine, Load — and the connectors an analyst reaches for most: folders, the web, and databases.

skills.name: Combining Queries: Merge, Append & Unpivot
skills.description: The three moves that turn several ragged tables into one clean one: join sideways, stack vertically, and flatten wide layouts into long ones.

skills.name: Shaping Data: Custom Columns & the M Language
skills.description: Go beyond the point-and-click transforms by writing custom columns and reading the M code behind every step.

skills.name: Parameters & Refresh: Making Queries Reusable
skills.description: Parameterize a query so the same logic runs against a new file, date range or environment, then keep it current with refresh.

skills.name: Data Model, Relationships & Star Schema
skills.description: Load multiple tables into Excel's Data Model and connect them with real relationships instead of VLOOKUPs, using a star schema so it stays fast and simple.

skills.name: DAX Fundamentals: CALCULATE & Filter Context
skills.description: The one idea that unlocks DAX: every measure runs inside a filter context, and CALCULATE is how you change it.

skills.name: DAX Time Intelligence & Power Pivot Measures
skills.description: Purpose-built DAX functions for year-to-date, prior-period and year-over-year measures, on top of a proper date table.

skills.name: Calculated Fields, Calculated Items & GETPIVOTDATA
skills.description: Add a calculation directly inside a PivotTable, and pull a stable value out of one with a formula that survives layout changes.

skills.name: Grouping, Advanced Layouts & PivotTables from the Data Model
skills.description: Group raw dates and numbers into readable buckets, and build a PivotTable straight from the Data Model instead of a single table.

skills.name: Descriptive Statistics & the Analysis ToolPak
skills.description: Enable Excel's built-in statistics add-in and use it to generate a full summary — mean, median, std dev, kurtosis — in one pass instead of one formula at a time.

skills.name: Correlation & Regression
skills.description: Quantify whether two variables move together, then fit a line through them and read what the ToolPak's regression output is actually telling you.

skills.name: Hypothesis Testing in Excel
skills.description: Decide whether a difference between two groups is likely real, using a t-test and a properly interpreted p-value.

skills.name: Moving Averages & Seasonality
skills.description: Smooth a noisy series with a moving average, then separate the seasonal pattern from the underlying trend.

skills.name: FORECAST.ETS & the Forecast Sheet
skills.description: Let Excel's exponential-smoothing engine project a time series forward automatically, with a confidence interval attached.

skills.name: Setting Up Solver: Objective, Variables & Constraints
skills.description: Translate a real optimization question — what mix maximizes profit? — into an objective cell, variable cells and constraints Solver can work with.

skills.name: Solver Methods & Sensitivity Reports
skills.description: Pick the right solving method for the shape of your problem, then read the sensitivity report to see how robust the optimal answer really is.

skills.name: Analytical Chart Types: Histogram, Box Plot, Pareto, Scatter & Waterfall
skills.description: Five chart types built to answer a specific analytical question — distribution, spread, the vital few causes, relationship, and the walk from one total to another.

skills.name: Interactive Dashboards: Slicers, Timelines & Layout
skills.description: Turn a set of PivotTables and charts into a single-page dashboard a reader can filter themselves, without touching a formula.

skills.name: Getting Started with Python in Excel
skills.description: Write your first =PY formula and see Python run in the cloud against your worksheet data, no separate install required.

skills.name: Python for Analysis: pandas & Visualization
skills.description: Use the pandas, Matplotlib and Seaborn libraries that ship with Python in Excel to do analysis a formula alone would struggle with.

skills.name: Large Data & Performance
skills.description: Diagnose why a big workbook has gone slow, and the specific habits — volatile functions, full-column references, unfolded queries — that usually cause it.

skills.name: Excel to Power BI: Making the Jump
skills.description: Recognize the signals that a report has outgrown Excel, and see how far a Power Pivot Data Model already carries over to Power BI.

skills.name: Capstone: End-to-End Analysis Project
skills.description: Every skill in this track, applied in sequence to one dataset: clean it, load it, model it, analyze it, forecast it, and present it on one page.

skills.name: Keyboard-Only Navigation & Shortcuts
skills.description: Move around a workbook, select ranges, and switch sheets without ever touching the mouse — the baseline speed habit every finance role expects.

skills.name: Excel Options & Number Formats for Model Setup
skills.description: Configure calculation settings and number formats before you start building, so the model behaves predictably later.

skills.name: Time Value of Money Functions
skills.description: PV, FV, PMT, RATE and NPER — the five functions behind every loan, annuity and savings calculation.

skills.name: NPV, IRR, XIRR & MIRR
skills.description: Discount a stream of cash flows and find its rate of return — and know when regular NPV/IRR are wrong.

skills.name: Depreciation & Date Functions for Models
skills.description: Depreciate an asset three different ways and handle the date arithmetic that schedules and debt models depend on.

skills.name: Lookup Formulas: INDEX/MATCH, XLOOKUP & Why to Avoid OFFSET/INDIRECT
skills.description: Robust ways to pull a value from a table, and why OFFSET and INDIRECT are a modelling liability even though they can do the same job.

skills.name: SUMIFS, SUMPRODUCT & Conditional Aggregation
skills.description: Summing and counting by condition — the two workhorse functions behind every summary schedule and check row.

skills.name: Dynamic Arrays, LET & LAMBDA
skills.description: Modern Excel 365 formulas that spill results across a range and let you name and reuse logic inside a single formula.

skills.name: Revenue & Opex Build
skills.description: Forecast the top of the income statement from explicit business drivers instead of a hardcoded growth rate.

skills.name: Working Capital Schedule
skills.description: Forecast operating assets and liabilities as a percent of sales or COGS, and turn that into the change in NWC the cash flow statement needs.

skills.name: PP&E / Capex & Depreciation Schedule
skills.description: Roll forward gross PP&E, accumulated depreciation and net PP&E so capex, depreciation and the balance sheet all reconcile.

skills.name: Building a Debt Schedule
skills.description: Track each tranche of debt — beginning balance, draws, repayments, interest, ending balance — across every forecast period.

skills.name: Circular References, Circuit Breakers & Iterative Calculation
skills.description: Interest calculated on an average or ending debt balance feeds back into the cash flow that determines that same balance — handle the resulting circularity deliberately, not by accident.

skills.name: Discounted Cash Flow Model
skills.description: Project unlevered free cash flow, discount it at WACC, and add a terminal value to get an intrinsic enterprise value.

skills.name: Trading & Transaction Comps Table
skills.description: Value a company against what the market actually pays for similar businesses, using a clean, formula-driven comps table.

skills.name: LBO Model From Scratch
skills.description: Fund an acquisition mostly with debt, run the target's cash flow through a debt paydown, and solve for the sponsor's return at exit.

skills.name: Merger Model & Accretion/Dilution Analysis
skills.description: Combine an acquirer and target's financials, layer in the deal's financing, and test whether the combined EPS beats the acquirer's standalone EPS.

skills.name: Monte Carlo Fundamentals: RAND, NORM.INV & Distributions
skills.description: Turn a single-point forecast into a probability distribution using nothing but built-in Excel functions.

skills.name: Data-Table-Driven Simulation & Tornado Charts
skills.description: Repeat a randomized model thousands of times without an add-in, and rank which assumption actually drives the spread of outcomes.

skills.name: Football Field & Valuation Range Charts
skills.description: Show several valuation methodologies' low-high ranges on one chart, the way a banker's fairness-opinion deck does.

skills.name: Waterfall / Bridge Charts
skills.description: Show how a starting number is bridged to an ending number through a series of positive and negative steps.

skills.name: Variance Charts (Actual vs Budget)
skills.description: Make a budget-vs-actual gap visible at a glance instead of buried in a table of numbers.

skills.name: Finance Dashboard Design Principles
skills.description: The layout and formatting choices that make a dashboard readable in thirty seconds instead of five minutes.

skills.name: Building an Excel Finance Dashboard
skills.description: Wire slicers and dynamic titles into a dashboard so one control updates every chart and KPI on the page at once.

skills.name: VBA Fundamentals for Analysts
skills.description: Record your first macro, then read and edit the code it generates in the Visual Basic Editor.

skills.name: Loops, Automation & Report Generation
skills.description: Repeat an action across a range, a collection of sheets, or a folder of files instead of doing it by hand.

skills.name: User-Defined Functions (UDFs) for Finance
skills.description: Write your own worksheet function in VBA when nothing built into Excel does the calculation you need.

skills.name: Power Query Fundamentals for Finance Data
skills.description: Connect, transform and load data through Power Query's editor instead of formulas or copy-paste.

skills.name: Cleaning & Combining GL Extracts and Bank Statements
skills.description: Turn a messy general ledger or bank export into a clean, analysis-ready table every time it refreshes.

skills.name: Multi-Entity / Multi-File Consolidations
skills.description: Combine a folder of identically structured entity or period files into one consolidated table that updates itself.

skills.name: Timed Modelling Speed Drills
skills.description: Deliberate, timed repetition — not more new material — is what actually makes shortcuts and formulas automatic.

skills.name: Practice Case Studies & Modelling Tests
skills.description: Everything from this track, applied under a clock, against a case study you haven't seen before.

skills.name: 13-Week Cash Flow Modeling
skills.description: Can build a direct-method 13-week cash flow model from scratch, set a defensible minimum cash threshold with a liquidity bridge and variance process, and stress-test the model for a lender presentation.

skills.name: Distressed Valuation & Credit Analysis
skills.description: Can value a distressed company under liquidation and going-concern scenarios, map the capital structure to identify the fulcrum security, and build a recovery waterfall across claim classes.

skills.name: Why Companies Fail — Liquidity, Solvency & the Distress Cycle
skills.description: Distinguish a liquidity problem from a solvency problem, learn the early warning signs of financial distress, and understand the cycle that pulls a company from underperformance toward restructuring.

skills.name: The Restructuring Industry Landscape — Consulting Firms, RX Banks & Law Firms
skills.description: Map the players — turnaround consultancies like A&M and FTI, restructuring investment banks like PJT and Houlihan Lokey, and the law firms that run the courtroom side of a case.

skills.name: Breaking In — Case Competitions, TMA, and the Audit-to-Restructuring Pipeline
skills.description: Learn the real, recurring paths into the industry: the Big 4 audit/valuation/FDD-to-restructuring pipeline, TMA and TMA NextGen as a genuine student differentiator, and named case competitions that award real interviews.

skills.name: Chapter 11 vs. Chapter 7 vs. Out-of-Court Workouts
skills.description: Compare reorganization under Chapter 11, liquidation under Chapter 7, and negotiated out-of-court workouts — and understand why a company and its advisors choose one path over another.

skills.name: DIP Financing, Creditor Committees & Claims Administration
skills.description: Learn how debtor-in-possession financing keeps a bankrupt company running, how the official creditors' committee operates, and how proofs of claim and bar dates administer who gets to be paid.

skills.name: Absolute Priority, Cramdown & a Brief Look at UK Administration/CVA
skills.description: Understand the absolute priority rule and how a plan gets 'crammed down' over an objecting class, then contrast the US process with UK administration and Company Voluntary Arrangements.

skills.name: Building a 13-Week Cash Flow Model From Scratch
skills.description: Build a direct-method, weekly cash flow model from receipts and disbursements — the exact tool A&M and FTI use as the entry point to almost every restructuring engagement.

skills.name: Minimum Cash, Liquidity Bridges & Variance Analysis
skills.description: Set a defensible minimum cash threshold, build a liquidity bridge that ties covenant headroom to the forecast, and run the weekly actual-vs-forecast variance process that keeps the model credible.

skills.name: Stress-Testing and Presenting a 13-Week Cash Flow to Lenders
skills.description: Build base, downside, and stress scenarios into the model, then present it to a skeptical lender group who will challenge every assumption behind it.

skills.name: Liquidation Value vs. Going-Concern Value
skills.description: Learn the liquidation analysis that sets the 'floor' recovery for creditors, and understand when a business is worth more sold whole and operating than broken apart.

skills.name: Capital Structure, Debt Tranches & the Fulcrum Security
skills.description: Map a distressed company's capital stack from senior secured debt down to equity, and identify the fulcrum security — the tranche where enterprise value runs out and control converts to equity.

skills.name: Recovery Analysis & the Distribution Waterfall
skills.description: Build a recovery waterfall that ranks every class of claim by priority and pays them out until enterprise value is exhausted — the core output of any distressed valuation exercise.

skills.name: Diagnosing the Business — Cost Structure & EBITDA Bridge Analysis
skills.description: Break a company's cost base down into its real drivers and build an EBITDA bridge that explains, bar by bar, exactly what moved profitability between two periods.

skills.name: Building the Long-Term Business Plan
skills.description: Translate the diagnostic and the 13-week forecast into a multi-year business plan that underpins valuation, lender negotiations, and the plan of reorganization itself.

skills.name: Case Studies in Real-World Corporate Turnarounds
skills.description: Study well-documented turnarounds and liquidations — American Airlines, Hertz, and Toys 'R' Us among them — to see how the tools in this course played out in practice.

skills.name: The Restructuring Interview — Technical Case Prep
skills.description: Prepare for an interview process that is unusually technical and light on behavioral questions — candidates report Excel tests and simplified cash-flow model walkthroughs, not case-study frameworks.

skills.name: Positioning Your Story — From Audit/Finance Background to Restructuring
skills.description: Turn a Big 4 audit, FDD, or valuation background into a convincing restructuring narrative — what transfers directly, what you need to backfill, and how to frame the pivot.

skills.name: Certifications & Career Pathway — CIRA, CTP, CFA
skills.description: Understand CIRA, CTP, and the CFA charter as career-progression credentials you pursue once you're in the industry, not requirements to break in.

skills.name: Geospatial Data & Python — GeoPandas, Shapefiles & Mapping Fundamentals
skills.description: What geospatial (vector) data actually is, and how to read, manipulate, and map shapefiles and GeoJSON with geopandas — including basic spatial joins.

skills.name: GIS Visualization Platforms — ArcGIS, QGIS, CARTO & Alteryx
skills.description: What each tool in a location-analytics stack is actually for — desktop GIS mapping in ArcGIS/QGIS, cloud-based dashboards in CARTO, and no-code data prep with built-in predictive modeling in Alteryx.

skills.name: Location Analytics in Practice — Retail Site Selection, Store Footprint & Applied Predictive Modeling
skills.description: How consulting and advisory firms actually use this toolkit — retail site-selection and store-footprint optimization, using Gradient Boosting and Random Forest to predict foot traffic and demand.

skills.name: The Chapter 11 Process
skills.description: Can walk a Chapter 11 case end-to-end: what first-day motions actually ask for, what's really negotiated in a DIP financing agreement, and how a plan of reorganization moves from draft through disclosure statement to confirmation.

skills.name: Creditor Priority & Legal Mechanisms
skills.description: Can recognize the specific Bankruptcy Code mechanisms that drive deal terms — Section 365 executory contracts, Section 363 sales, preference and fraudulent transfer actions, the absolute priority rule and cramdown, secured/unsecured creditor rights, and KEIP/KERP rules.

skills.name: The Automatic Stay — What Freezes the Moment a Case Is Filed
skills.description: Understand exactly what the automatic stay does and doesn't stop the instant a bankruptcy petition is filed, why it's called 'automatic,' and the statutory exceptions and relief-from-stay process that restructuring professionals need to recognize.

skills.name: Chapters 7, 11, and 15 — Liquidation, Reorganization, and Cross-Border Cases Compared
skills.description: Compare liquidation under Chapter 7, reorganization under Chapter 11, and the ancillary cross-border framework of Chapter 15 — and understand why the choice of chapter shapes everything that follows in a case.

skills.name: Who's in the Room — Debtor's Counsel, the UCC and Its Counsel, the U.S. Trustee, and the Judge
skills.description: Map the actual participants in a Chapter 11 case: debtor's counsel and its fiduciary duties, the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors and its own counsel, the U.S. Trustee's oversight role, and the bankruptcy judge.

skills.name: First-Day Motions and the First 30 Days of a Case
skills.description: Learn what first-day motions actually ask for — cash management, critical vendors, wages, utilities — and why the first-day hearing sets the tone for the entire case.

skills.name: DIP Financing Agreements — What's Actually in Them and Why Lenders Get Control
skills.description: Go inside an actual DIP credit agreement: budget covenants, milestones, roll-up provisions, priming liens, and the superpriority status that gives DIP lenders outsized leverage over the case.

skills.name: The Plan of Reorganization and Disclosure Statement — From Draft to Confirmation
skills.description: Follow a plan of reorganization from drafting through disclosure statement approval, creditor solicitation, voting, and the confirmation hearing that determines whether a debtor emerges from Chapter 11.

skills.name: Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases (Section 365) — Assume, Assign, or Reject
skills.description: Understand the debtor's powerful Section 365 right to cherry-pick which contracts and leases to keep, cure and assume, assign to a third party, or reject — and what that means for counterparties.

skills.name: Section 363 Sales — Stalking Horse Bids, Auctions, and Selling Assets Free and Clear
skills.description: Learn how a Section 363 sale lets a debtor sell assets outside a plan, free and clear of liens and claims, through a stalking-horse bid, court-supervised auction, and sale hearing.

skills.name: Preferences and Fraudulent Transfers (Sections 547/548) — Clawing Back Pre-Bankruptcy Payments
skills.description: Understand how a trustee or debtor in possession can claw back payments made shortly before filing under the preference rules of Section 547 and the actual and constructive fraud tests of Section 548.

skills.name: The Absolute Priority Rule and Cramdown, in Depth
skills.description: Go beyond the one-line definition: study how the absolute priority rule actually gets litigated, what 'fair and equitable' requires class by class, the new value exception, and how a plan gets crammed down over an objecting class.

skills.name: Secured vs. Unsecured Creditor Rights and Contractual Subordination
skills.description: Understand what actually separates a secured claim from an unsecured one in a bankruptcy case, and how contractual subordination agreements between creditors get enforced under Section 510.

skills.name: Executive Retention Pay in Bankruptcy — KEIP/KERP Rules and Why They're Controversial
skills.description: Learn the BAPCPA-era rules under Section 503(c) that sharply limit retention bonuses (KERPs) but allow incentive plans tied to difficult-to-reach milestones (KEIPs) — and why courts scrutinize the difference so closely.

skills.name: Chapter 15 — How Cross-Border Insolvency Actually Works
skills.description: Understand how a foreign representative petitions a U.S. court for recognition of a foreign proceeding as 'main' or 'non-main,' and what powers and protections recognition actually confers.

skills.name: UK Administration, CVAs, and Schemes of Arrangement — A Working Comparison to Chapter 11
skills.description: Build a working comparison of the major UK restructuring tools — Administration, Company Voluntary Arrangements, Schemes of Arrangement, and the newer Part 26A Restructuring Plan — against U.S. Chapter 11.

skills.name: Out-of-Court Workouts and Exchange Offers — The Legal Mechanics When You Avoid Court
skills.description: Learn how companies restructure debt entirely outside of bankruptcy court through negotiated workouts and exchange offers, and the securities-law and intercreditor mechanics that make them work.

skills.name: How Restructuring Advisors and Lawyers Actually Divide the Work
skills.description: Understand the practical division of labor on a real case between debtor's counsel, the investment bank or turnaround consultant, and the chief restructuring officer — and how the best teams coordinate.

skills.name: Adversary Proceedings and Bankruptcy Litigation Basics
skills.description: Learn what turns a bankruptcy case into a lawsuit: the categories of disputes that must be filed as adversary proceedings under Rule 7001, and how that litigation track runs alongside the main case.

skills.name: Reading a First-Day Declaration and Other Real Case Filings
skills.description: Read an actual first-day declaration from a major, well-documented Chapter 11 case and learn how to extract the business history, capital structure, and narrative that every other filing in the case builds on.
